# The One Big Idea {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

When you "talk to AI", you talk to **two things**

## Session 1 Left a Question {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="bridge" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.2em;"}
AI **predicts** the next word. It doesn't "know" facts.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-size: 1.2em; margin-top: 1em;"}
So how does it ever feel like it **remembers you**?
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-important}
## Today's keystone
Everything else in this course hangs off one insight: you're really talking to
**two layers stacked together**.
:::

# The Model Layer {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

The brain in a jar

## A Brilliant Brain — With Amnesia {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="brain" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #9B8EC0;"}
A brilliant graduate's brain floating in a **jar**. It has read most of the internet,
so it's clever — but it has **total amnesia**.
:::

. . .

::: {.incremental}
- Knows nothing about *you*, your company, or what you said five minutes ago
- The instant it finishes answering, it **forgets everything**
- All it does is **predict the next word** from the text it was just handed
:::

## What It Really Is {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.15em;"}
The model is **stateless**. It does not "remember" and it does not "look things up".
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-note}
## The same prediction engine from Session 1
When it doesn't know, it predicts a plausible-sounding word **anyway** — that's a
*hallucination*.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
Anything you want it to "know", you must **hand it every single time**.
:::

# The App Layer {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

The office around the brain

## We Build an Office {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="office" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7;"}
The brain in a jar can't open files or remember your name. So we build an **office**
around it: filing cabinets, a notebook, a standing to-do list.
:::

. . .

Every time you ask for something, the office **gathers the relevant pages and hands
them to the brain** along with your request — then files the answer back.

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
The brain still has amnesia. The *office* is what makes it feel like it remembers.
:::

## What It Really Is {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.1em;"}
The **app** (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, the **Hermes** agent…) is the software
wrapped around the model.
:::

. . .

It **stores your information in files / a directory** and **re-sends the relevant parts
on every request**.

. . .

::: {.callout-tip}
## The features you've seen
"Memory", "Projects", "Custom Instructions" are all just the **app** doing this
gathering-and-resending for you.
:::

## The Sentence to Remember {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="background: #00C9A7; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.1em;"}
The model **knows nothing and forgets everything**;
the app **re-sends what matters on every request.**
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 1em;"}
Every feature in this course is just the app getting smarter about **what to re-send.**
:::

# What "Context" Really Is {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

The pages on the brain's desk

## Context = the Desk {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="context" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #9B8EC0;"}
**Context** is everything the office stacks on the brain's desk before it starts —
your request **plus** the background pages it needs to do the job well.
:::

. . .

Your instructions, pasted documents, standing rules, relevant memory — the model's
**entire world** for that one request.

## The Big Reframe {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.2em;"}
Output quality is mostly a **context problem**, not a **smartness problem**.
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-important}
## What this means for you
A weak answer usually means weak **context**, not a weak model.
**"Give it context" is the whole skill.**
:::

# The Desk Has Limits {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #FF7A5C, #1C355E)"}

The context window

## Why Long Chats "Forget" {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="window" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C;"}
The brain's desk has a **fixed size**. You can only fit so many pages on it at once.
Pile on too much and **older pages fall off the edge**.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
That's the **context window** — and it's why a long conversation starts losing the
thread from the beginning.
:::

## The Payoff: Saved Beats Re-Pasted {auto-animate=true}

::: {.callout-tip}
## The rule
**Saved instructions beat re-pasting.**
:::

The app puts the important pages back on the desk for you **every time**, so they never
fall off the edge.

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-style: italic; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
This is the entire reason `CLAUDE.md`, Projects, and Memory exist — coming on Day 2.
:::

# One More Word: "Script" {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

Demystified before Day 2

## A Script Is a Recipe Card {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="script" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7;"}
A **recipe card** of steps, written down once, so the job runs the same way every
time — whether a person or the agent follows it.
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-note}
## Not a programmer thing
A "script" is just *"do these steps, in this order, every time."*
**You never write code in this course** — you describe the steps in plain language.
:::

# It All Clicks {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

The payoff

## The Office Getting Smarter {auto-animate=true}

Once you see the two layers, the whole Day-2 toolkit is just **the app deciding what
to re-send**:

::: {.incremental}
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — standing instructions, re-sent every time
- **Project** — pulls *the right folder's* pages onto the desk
- **Memory** — facts about you, re-sent when relevant
- **Skill** — a saved recipe the app runs on command
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
None of it is magic. It's all **context management**.
:::

# Build: Your Context Pack {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

Raw material for Day 2

## Write the Pages the Brain Needs {auto-animate=true}

Pick one task from your **Automation Backlog** (Session 1). Write its **context pack** —
the standing facts the AI would need **every single time** to do it well:

::: {.incremental}
- Who you are and your role
- The tone and format you always want
- The rules that never change (audience, do's and don'ts)
- The background facts the task always assumes
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip}
## Keep it
On Day 2 this becomes your first **`CLAUDE.md`** — paste it once, never re-type it again.
:::

Which layer do you fix?

## Quiz — Question 1 {auto-animate=true}

The AI gets the **tone wrong every single time** — too casual for your board.

Which layer?

. . .

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
::: {style="background: #00C9A7; color: white; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center;"}
**The App Layer** — fix your **standing instructions**. It's a re-send problem,
not the brain.
:::
:::

## Quiz — Question 2 {auto-animate=true}

The AI cites **"Article 214"** of a law — and the article doesn't exist.

Which layer?

. . .

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
::: {style="background: #9B8EC0; color: white; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center;"}
**The Model Layer** — the brain **guessed**. Ground it in a real source and
**verify** (Session 4).
:::
:::

## Key Takeaways {.sdaia-dark background-color="#1C355E"}

::: {.incremental}
1. **Two layers** — the model (brain) and the app (office) stacked together
2. **The brain has amnesia** — stateless, predicts the next word, forgets everything
3. **The office re-sends context** — that's what makes AI feel like it remembers
4. **Quality is a context problem** — give it the right pages, get the right answer
5. **The desk is finite** — saved instructions beat re-pasting
6. **Day 2 = the office getting smarter** about what to re-send
:::
